discovery: Discovery and establishment of magnetoelectric multiferroics: coupling of magnetism and ferroelectricity in correlated oxides

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics: correlated electron oxides and multiferroics
motivation: Magnetism and ferroelectricity were long thought to be mutually exclusive. The nominees overturned this and created a new field. Spaldin explained theoretically why the two orders rarely coexist in transition-metal oxides and showed how to get around it. Ramesh made epitaxial BiFeO3 films with large room-temperature polarization and demonstrated electric-field control of antiferromagnetic domains and of exchange-coupled magnetism. Tokura discovered that spiral spin order induces ferroelectricity in TbMnO3, so that a magnetic field can switch polarization. This revealed spin-driven ferroelectricity and its spin-orbit microscopic origin. Together they turned a curiosity into a broad discipline that unites correlated-electron physics, symmetry, first-principles theory and atomic-scale thin-film growth. It now underpins work on magnetoelectric control, low-power spintronic memory and logic, and topological spin textures. Few developments in quantum materials have reshaped both fundamental understanding and device thinking so much.
